paper: OSTI 3374709 — Hedlof, Barnes, Groenewald et al., Phys. Plasmas 33, 053902 (2026), semi-implicit ES-PIC verification

open_questions.q: Does the ~10% error observed at ωpe·Δt = 16 reflect a real breakdown of the SIPIC effective-dielectric down-shift (Eq. 16) at extreme step sizes, or is it a diagnostic artifact of the Hann-windowed FFT + parabolic sub-bin interpolation with only ~6 samples per down-shifted oscillation?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §4 C1 table shows monotone 3.3/0.9/3.9/1.9% agreement for ωpe·Δt ∈ {1,2,4,8} and a jump to 10.2% at ωpe·Δt = 16. §3 diagnostic explicitly uses Hann window + parabolic sub-bin interpolation; the caveat notes 'only ~6 samples per down-shifted oscillation' at the extreme step. The replication did not attempt to separate scheme error from diagnostic error.
open_questions.next_steps: Run the same ωpe·Δt = 16 case with (a) 2–4× longer time series to add spectral resolution, (b) alternative estimators (Prony/matrix-pencil, sinusoidal least-squares fit) and (c) multiple RNG seeds and particle counts to get uncertainty bars. If all estimators agree at ~10% error, the departure is real; if it shrinks toward ~1–4%, it was diagnostic.

open_questions.q: Which reading of the paper's κ-notation is the one the authors actually implemented in WarpX/Aleph — the literal Eq. 12/13 (κ = 1/F, ω² = ωp²/κ, i.e. up-shift) or the physically-consistent down-shift matching Eq. 16 and Fig. 1?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §4 discrepancies flags a paper-internal inversion: Eq. 12/13 written literally gives ω² = ωp²·F (up-shift), which contradicts the Eq. 16 text ('reduced frequency') and the downward contours of Fig. 1. The replication chose the down-shift reading because it is physically consistent and matches the numerical trend, but it is a judgement call, not a confirmation from the authors or the reference codes.
open_questions.next_steps: (1) Ask the authors directly which formula went into the WarpX/Aleph implementation. (2) Independently rebuild both readings in the from-scratch code and check which one is consistent with the paper's own Fig. 1 dispersion contours. (3) If WarpX/Aleph source is available, inspect the field-operator code path to see the sign/exponent of κ used at runtime.

open_questions.q: Does the paper's claim that hybrid physics is essentially unaffected (C4: upper/lower hybrid frequencies shift only via ωpe,SI, Eqs. 19–20) survive an independent test in a magnetized 2D setting?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §2 lists C4 as testable but 'No (out of scope for 1D core)' in this replication. The 1D ES-PIC used here has no B-field, so hybrid modes cannot form. The paper's §III.B is a substantive part of its verification argument that has not been independently checked here.
open_questions.next_steps: Extend the from-scratch code to 2D3V ES-PIC with an imposed uniform B-field, seed upper- and lower-hybrid mode perturbations, and compare the extracted frequencies against Eqs. 19–20 with ωpe,SI substituted per Eq. 16. Sweep the same C_SI = 4 and a range of ωpe·Δt to check that only ωpe is down-shifted and the cyclotron branch is untouched.

open_questions.q: Is the paper's energy-conservation claim (C5: total energy change < 2.5% over a full run, with SIPIC ≈ ECPIC behavior) reproducible in an independent implementation, or does it depend on details of the WarpX/Aleph time integrator that were not spelled out in the paper?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §2 lists C5 as tested='No (Fig. 2, requires full WarpX/Aleph runs).' The replication's leapfrog + spectral Poisson + Eqs. 9–10 operator was verified against the dispersion claim C1 but was not exercised for long-time energy behavior; no energy trace is reported.
open_questions.next_steps: Add diagnostics for kinetic energy Σ½m v², electrostatic field energy ½∫ε₀E²dx, and their sum over full-length runs at each ωpe·Δt in the sweep. Compare the fractional drift ΔE_tot/E_tot against the paper's 2.5% target. If the 1D leapfrog+FFT scheme cannot hit 2.5%, the claim depends on additional integrator machinery (Boris push, particle sub-stepping, symplectic corrections) that the paper should specify.

open_questions.q: How does the SIPIC scheme behave for kinetic (Landau-damped) modes at large ωpe·Δt (C6, §III.C), where the paper claims damping rates are preserved — does the effective-dielectric operator distort the resonance structure that produces Landau damping when Δt is far larger than the natural plasma period?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §2 lists C6 as testable but 'No (out of scope).' The replication's cold-limit setup (vth = 0) was chosen precisely to isolate C1 and therefore cannot produce Landau damping at all. The paper's §III.C is a nontrivial claim: preserving a subtle kinetic effect while suppressing the plasma wave is not automatic.
open_questions.next_steps: Switch the from-scratch code to a warm Maxwellian plasma (finite vth, kλ_D chosen for measurable damping), seed a small-amplitude Langmuir wave, and extract γ from the exponential envelope of the mode-1 electric-field amplitude. Sweep both C_SI (0 vs 4) and ωpe·Δt to check whether the fitted γ matches the analytic Landau rate independent of Δt, or degrades as ωpe·Δt grows beyond the explicit limit.
